This is mainly because the lamellar α phase hinders the dislocation movement in the ﬁrst stage. Many dislocation accumulation and entanglement are formed at the α/β interface, resulting in peak stress significantly higher than that of the equiaxed α phase [43].
With the dislocation density increasing, the lamellar bending/kinking is responsible for the flow softening.
the heat generated by plastic deformation is difﬁcult to dissipate, which leads to a signiﬁcant increase in the center temperature of the sample
when the activation energy is close to the self-diffusion activation energy, DRV is the main softening mechanism
In the DRX process, the LAGBs transform to the HAGBs by grain rotation and diffusion flow
the high m value indicates that grain boundary sliding may be the main mechanism contributing to superplastic deformation
